data.body: Landed as Gerrit change 3105, commit f3cb9223d8c (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved). Reproduced first with real events, no git mocks: an event committed after the sweep's --no-merges position map was built, and an event only a merge commit adds, both made _build_authorship_ledger call resolve_event_commit / resolve_position_commit while .ticket-write.lock.d existed. The existing no-walk-under-lock test passed anyway because it watched only the map builders. Measured on this host's 300,142-commit tickets clone: one store-wide resolver walk took 140.42 s and 142.43 s against the resolver's 30 s timeout; the production server's figure was NOT measured and its map-miss rate is unknown (task 08c8-6262-3f5a-4110). Fix: preresolve_unmapped_positions resolves missing positions before each ticket's locked fold; an unattributable position, including a timeout, carries an empty in-map marker that is persisted as JSON null, so no walk runs under the lock and the ledger equals today's. 5 of the 6 new tests fail on the old code; 15 sweep tests and 292 compaction/authorship/ledger tests pass. make verify locally: only the 17 known pandoc failures, no errors; Linux CI green. Not fixed here, by design: a merge-only event can never be attributed by these resolvers, so its ledger commit stays null as before. Review advisory (non-blocking, text truncated in the bot message): the per-ticket map copy and markers not carried across tickets cost time outside the lock; not changed, since a new patch set would reset the votes. Candidate follow-up if the sweep is still slow.
